title: Shreveport bandmates and the Kilgore keg house
summary: He lists Harry James and others in the Shreveport band, then describes a rough east Texas oil-boom keg house in Kilgore where he got his head busted and left.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Well, it was a great bunch of guys and we -- let's see, Harry James was in that band for awhile. And oh, Tommy Goslin and Truitte Jones and Curtis Hurt and, oh, the arranger -- oh, he later arranged a lot for the Bob Crosby band -- oh, a saxophone player. I can't think of his name. He's been an important arranger. I'll think of it. But he was in the band, he was writing arrangements for it, and it was quite a pleasant time. Of course that came to an end and I went to work in -- over in the east Texas oil fields, in what they called a keg house, and -- Kilgore, Texas. It was a boom town, an oil boom town. If you've never been in one you have no idea. It's -- the people there, the streets were mud. In the keg house you kicked the band off at 8:00 o'clock and you didn't quit playing until 3:00 o'clock in the morning. And the booze was about two hours old. They had nothing but sugar whiskey and they had it in these fruit jars, and everybody was walking around with a mark on the bridge of their nose

from drinking out of the fruit jars. And there was a continuous fight going on there all the time. A real hard, rough job, and everything was very expensive. When it would rain the streets were so bad there was guys that made a living, they'd charge you fifty bucks to carry you across the street, because the mud got so deep, that east Texas red clay.
Yeah, I know about that, but --
Yeah, I got my head busted with a bottle down there, wound up in the pokey, and got out of there and got out of town.
Wow. How long were you there altogether?
I must have been there about a month.
And you went there from Shreveport?
How long were you in Shreveport?
Well, I was at Shreveport a couple of times. This was in between. This was after the first time. I went back to New York after that.
From Texas, yeah. After you get your head busted in, I said, maybe I'd better go back to New York.
